tips_en: I'd recommend reading Paper 2 (OPSA) first, as it presents the most striking finding—that teacher distillation may be largely unnecessary and a simple entropy-adaptive negative advantage scheme suffices—challenging a widely held assumption in LLM post-training. A nice thread connects all three papers: Paper 1 and Paper 3 both rely on RL post-training stages (modality-aware feedback and GRPO, respectively), so Paper 2's insights about the role (or irrelevance) of teacher supervision and the importance of low-probability token suppression could meaningfully inform how those RL components are designed.
tips_zh: 建议优先阅读第二篇（OPSA），因为它提出了一个最令人惊讶的发现——教师蒸馏可能并非必需，仅靠基于熵的自适应负优势机制就能取得更好效果——这挑战了LLM后训练中被广泛接受的假设。三篇论文之间有一条有趣的脉络：第一篇和第三篇都依赖RL后训练阶段（分别是模态感知反馈和GRPO），因此第二篇关于教师监督作用（或不必要性）以及低概率token抑制重要性的洞见，可能对设计这些RL组件具有启发意义。
